subject: CatalyzeAI — SLO fit, model constraints, and ops/runbook request
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Anna Bae <anna@catalyze.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — latency/throughput goals and next technical steps

Anna — thanks for a great call earlier. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we have alignment before Connor and I scope a POC: 

Key customer pain (as discussed):
- Unpredictable tail latency: p95 currently ~500–650ms for short (<=128 token) responses during peak.
- Queueing under bursty traffic — backend spikes pushing request queuing and CPU throttling.
- Cost tensions: current infra spend for inference at scale is high; team wants to get to lower unit cost without sacrificing latency.
- Some generation quality drift on safety/format constraints vs. in-house prompts.

Goals you shared:
- Target p95 latency <=200ms for short (<=512 token) responses on 95% of user-facing routes.
- Sustained throughput target: 120 req/s with 5% headroom for burst traffic.
- Support for longer generations up to ~2k tokens with graceful degradation (fall back to cheaper model variant).
- Deployment must be within their AWS account (VPC peering), SOC 2 evidence, and KMS integration.

Model/ops constraints (from your description):
- Preference for an Llama-2-derived 70B quantized variant for best quality, but open to hybrid approach (smaller low-latency model for short responses + larger for long-form).
- Customer cannot send raw logs outside their VPC; they can provide sanitized metrics and samples.

Immediate asks / agreed next steps:
1) Connor to propose a two-path topology (low-latency path + batch/throughput path) and sketch resource sizing.
2) Anna to share: a) a JSONL of 100 sample queries representative of p95 traffic, b) anonymized p95/p99 metrics for the last two peak days, and c) contact for procurement/SecOps.
3) Sean/Connor to prepare a high-level cost/latency estimate and runbook outline for a 6-week POC (target follow-up by Thursday).

Attachments: I'm including the short call export we recorded (see attachment stub). Connor — tagging you for the topology sketch & any clarifying questions.

Thanks — Sean

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Anna Bae <anna@catalyze.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 17:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — latency/throughput goals and next technical steps

Sean / Anna — thanks, concise recap. A few technical notes and clarifying questions to make the POC sizing accurate: 

Notes / tentative topology (high level):
- Two-path serving:
  * Fast-path (low-latency): quantized 13B/30B model variants optimized for sub-200ms p95 on short inputs. These would run on pinned instances (low batch sizes, optimized kernels, async I/O) and use local KV cache for common prefixes.
  * Batch-path (throughput): the 70B quantized weights on multi-GPU colocation for efficient batching during longer generations. Autoscale based on queue depth and a routing policy.
- Smart routing: request short/priority routes to fast-path by length & endpoint tagging; fallback routing to batch-path when headroom is saturated.
- KV / prefix cache: useful if you have repeated prompts/templates. We'll need RTT budget to estimate cache hit savings.
- Failure modes: propose circuit-breaker to route to smaller model if p95 spikes >400ms for 3 consecutive minutes.

Sizing questions (please provide):
1) Typical average tokens per response for the high-volume endpoints (we only have target rate).
2) Percent of requests that are <=128 tokens vs >512 tokens (rough split).
3) Any requirements for function/tool calls / streaming? Streaming can change CPU/locking behavior.

Security/ops questions:
- KMS/HSM: we can integrate with your KMS in the VPC for key handling; need the contact and allowed key policies.
- Audit logs: we can mirror audit events to your S3 bucket; confirm retention requirement (30/90/365 days).

I'll draft a topology sketch and nominal instance counts + cost band for the POC. If Anna can drop the 100-sample jsonl and the two peak-day p95/p99 numbers, I can iterate on the sizing tonight.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com
From: Anna Bae <anna@catalyze.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 08:17:44 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — latency/throughput goals and next technical steps

Thanks Sean, Connor — this looks right. I've attached a sample set and a small export of our p95/p99 for the last two traffic spikes. A few clarifications: 

- Token split: ~72% of requests are under 128 tokens, ~22% in 128–512, ~6% >512.
- Peak concurrency: 180 concurrent sessions observed during the last peak window; sustained 120 req/s aligns with our telemetry.
- Streaming: we do use server-side streaming for a subset of routes (~15%), but the latency SLO applies to the initial token turn.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence will be handled by our SecOps — contact is secops@catalyze.ai. We can accept a VPC connector and private peering; doc links in the attachment.

Attachments: catalyze_sample_queries.jsonl (100 items), catalyze_call_export_20280522.csv (sanitized), contact sheet for SecOps.

Question: What's a realistic timeline for a POC that demonstrates p95 <=200ms for short-path traffic? Also curious about an approximate monthly cost delta to run both paths in the POC posture.

Best —

Subject: Internal next steps — CatalyzeAI POC scope & owner assignments

Connor / Monica — looping internal owners and converting the customer asks into a concrete plan. Pulling the items from the thread and Anna's attachments into action items: 

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Connor: Draft topology sketch (fast-path + batch-path), instance counts, KV cache approach, and initial cost band for a 6-week POC — due Thu 2028-05-25 EOD. Reference: catalyze_sample_queries.jsonl for token distribution. (owner: connor@redwood.com)
- Monica: Prepare security checklist for VPC peering and KMS integration; draft the SOC2 evidence handoff and S3 audit mirror instructions — due Fri 2028-05-26. (owner: monica@redwood.com)
- Sean: Coordinate procurement contact, finalize POC mutual action plan, and schedule technical deep-dive with Catalyze's SecOps for next Tuesday. Send HubSpot update and proposed SOW template. (owner: sean@redwood.com)

POC rough timeline suggestion (subject to confirmation):
- Week 0: access + sanitized sample ingestion + topology validation.
- Week 1–2: fast-path deployment + smoke tests against sample queries.
- Week 3–4: batch-path sizing and warm-up; routing policy tuning.
- Week 5–6: live traffic test with controlled ramp, SLO validation, and handoff runbook.

I've added the Drive & HubSpot links to the thread (see metadata). Connor — once you post the topology sketch I'll pull together a short cost memo for the customer. Monica — please add any security blockers to the shared doc.

Thanks — Sean
